title: Catalog GLBs are not byte-reproducible: bevel output order follows pointer addresses
evidence: Building --only '^(console|desk)_' twice into two directories gave 26 of 30 differing GLBs (same vertex positions, different index buffers). _tag collected bmesh faces/edges in Python sets (address order) and bmesh.ops.bevel orders its result by pointer, so the exported vertex/index order changed per run (door_medical, console_weapons, desk_* ...). arch.canonicalize existed only for the arch assets.
impact: Every rebuild rewrites hundreds of binaries (noisy diffs, impossible to review), CI cannot ever compare GLBs, and the 'reproducible assets' claim in ARCH.md is false for the catalog.
fix: _tag uses insertion-ordered dict.fromkeys instead of sets; new kit.canonical_order() rebuilds each mesh with vertices sorted by (rounded) position, faces sorted by material and vertex ids, each face rotated to start at its lowest vertex, UVs and materials preserved; export() runs it before fix_zfight and again (welding) before writing.
resolution: All 1198 GLBs rebuilt twice with --jobs 4 and --jobs 3 are byte-identical (cmp over every file). tests/test_regress_assets.py::Deterministic builds a model subset twice (needs STARSHIP_BPY_PYTHON, skipped otherwise) and the new CI step 'Rebuilding gives byte-identical GLBs' does the same on every push.

title: sphere(clip_y) and prism() pass Python sets of BMesh elements to bmesh operators
evidence: `edges = {e for v in verts for e in v.link_edges}` / `faces = {f ...}` feed bisect_plane and `list({fc for ...})` feeds recalc_face_normals; set iteration order is memory-address order, so the operators saw their input in a different order on every run (same class of bug as A001).
impact: Dome and prism meshes (ceiling domes, wedges) could come out with a different triangulation/winding order between runs.
fix: Insertion-ordered list(dict.fromkeys(...)) in all three places.
resolution: tests/test_regress_assets.py::Deterministic::test_kit_never_iterates_sets_of_bmesh_elements greps kit.py for the set-comprehension pattern; build-twice test covers the output.

title: remove_doubles keeps an arbitrary one of two coincident opposite faces; invisible internal faces are exported
evidence: medbed_surgical_table and nozzle_rcs_thruster_cluster still differed between builds after the order fix: two touching boxes (md_sheet / brushed_alu slabs at z=0.3) leave two coincident, oppositely wound faces; remove_doubles dropped one of them, chosen by pointer order (material 3 in one run, 4 in the next). Float noise of 1e-8 in bevel/bisect vertices also differed per run.
impact: Non-reproducible output, plus hidden internal faces that cost triangles and can z-fight.
fix: canonical_order(weld=True) welds vertices on a 1e-5 grid itself, drops both faces of an opposing coincident pair (internal wall), keeps one of identical repeats, drops slivers, and snaps coordinates to 1e-5 (no -0.0).
resolution: Whole catalogue byte-identical across two builds (see A001); total triangles 1,104,397 -> 1,103,960 (internal faces removed).

title: 53 models violate their mount convention (floating, sunk or off the wall plane); the test allow-lists admitted them as 'known, NOT fixed'
evidence: tests/test_blender_tools.py ALLOW_FLOOR (45 ids, e.g. couch_bean_bag -0.021, loader_hover_pallet_jack +0.027, cylinder_portable_o2_unit +0.035), ALLOW_WALL (6, e.g. camera_palm_scanner -0.019, duct_plenum_damper_box -0.05), ALLOW_CEILING (2, planter_grow_light_bar_panel +0.03) plus tableware_teapot (table, +0.019). Every one was measured from godot/data/catalog.json.
impact: Props float 1-3.5 cm above the floor or sink into it/the wall, which shows as light leaks, z-fight against the deck and shadows that do not touch their object; layout clearances are computed from wrong bounds.
fix: kit.snap_origin() runs in export(): offsets below ORIGIN_SNAP (4.5 cm) of the mount plane are removed by shifting the model (floor/table y, wall z, ceiling top), larger ones (5 cm hover stretcher, 5 cm sunk damper box) are deliberate and kept.
resolution: Rebuilt catalogue: 53 -> 2 deliberate exceptions. tests/test_blender_tools.py allow-lists shrunk to those two and tests/test_regress_assets.py::MountOrigins asserts every model within 1.5 mm of its plane.

title: fix_zfight lifts the same shared vertices on every pass: small food items grow by up to 5.7 cm and no longer match the committed catalog
evidence: can_sixpack_cola: 12.3 cm tall in the committed catalog/GLB, 18.0 cm when rebuilt from the generator at HEAD (228 faces lifted over 8 passes, `moved` was filled but never read and the guard had been replaced by `if True:`); veg_cucumbers_sliced grew from 0.22 to 0.243 m wide, bottle_hip_flask_steel 0.032 -> 0.034 m. tests/test_food.py (sizes realistic / origins centred) failed on a fresh rebuild.
impact: The CI blender job (catalog comparison, 5 mm tolerance) fails for every rebuild; items drift in size and swell against their host table.
fix: A vertex is lifted at most once (`moved` is honoured), vertex/face indices are refreshed at the start of each pass (they were stale after bmesh ops), the lift direction is copied before vertices move.
resolution: can_sixpack_cola 12.6 cm, cucumbers 0.22 m after the fix; tests/test_regress_assets.py::ZfightLiftIsBounded plus the existing test_food size/origin tests pass on the rebuilt catalogue.

title: torus_prof outlines are wound clockwise while lathe() needs counter-clockwise: donuts, bagels and ice-cream rings are inside out
evidence: Closed-shell volume of the exported meshes is negative for bakery_bagel_poppy (-1.95e-4), bakery_donut_chocolate (-1.75e-4), bakery_donut_pink_sprinkles (-1.86e-4) and dessert_ice_cream_cone_double (two rings, -2.1e-5/-1.6e-5); every other lathe solid (cans etc.) uses the counter-clockwise profile (0,0),(r,0),(r,h),(0,h). The docstring claimed 'clockwise' which is what misled the food author.
impact: With back-face culling the outside of the donut/bagel/cone rings is invisible and their inside is lit with inverted normals.
fix: torus_prof reverses its point list (counter-clockwise, outside on the left); both docstrings corrected.
resolution: Rebuilt; a closed-shell volume scan over all 1198 GLBs finds 0 inverted shells. tests/test_regress_assets.py::NoInsideOutShells asserts positive volume for the four models.

title: door_cabin is geometrically identical to door_bulkhead (pure recolour)
evidence: Sorted vertex-position hash of all meshes is the same for door_bulkhead.glb and door_cabin.glb (the only duplicate pair among 1198 models, apart from the numeral-textured deck signs); the generator differs only by the paint/accent colours at index 0 and 4. CONVENTIONS.md: 'Every variant must look different ... not just a recolour'.
impact: Two catalogue entries (and two BOM line items) that are indistinguishable by shape.
fix: Cabin door gets a frosted privacy slit with a dark frame in each leaf and a door-number plate beside the frame.
resolution: tests/test_regress_assets.py::VariantsDiffer compares sorted vertex positions of every model sharing triangle count and size.

title: Blender job asserts `len(a) == 1000` but the catalog has 1198 models, and the comparison ignores triangles, solid, tags, mount_y and top_y
evidence: godot/data/catalog.json has 1198 entries (build_all.TARGET = 1198); the inline script `assert a.keys() == b.keys() and len(a) == 1000` therefore fails on every run. Step names still say '1000 models'. Only mount, category, size and bounds were compared (5 mm), so a changed triangle budget, top surface (table hosts) or tag set passed silently.
impact: The blender job is red (or, once the number is fixed, blind to most catalog drift).
fix: Count check is `>= 1198` against the id set; the comparison now covers mount, category, solid, tags, tris, mount_y, size, bounds and top_y; step names no longer hard-code a number.

lines: blender job, new step 'Rebuilding gives byte-identical GLBs'
title: CI has no reproducibility check for the generated GLBs although the docs claim determinism
evidence: ARCH.md/CONVENTIONS.md promise deterministic output but no step builds twice; A001 stayed unnoticed.
fix: New step builds a representative subset twice (different --jobs, textures copied from the first build) and `diff -r`s the models.
resolution: Step added to ci.yml; tests/test_regress_assets.py::DocsAndCiAgree asserts it exists.

title: Lint step exempts the whole components/ directory, hiding unused imports and redefinitions
evidence: `grep -v ... |^blender/starship/components/` removed every pyflakes finding of the 19 generator modules; unfiltered pyflakes reports an unused import in medical.py (`slats`) and foodkit.py (`bmesh`) plus ~45 dead stores. The same filter also swallowed 'unable to detect undefined names' only by accident.
impact: Real mistakes in 70% of the Python code base (the generators) can never fail CI.
fix: Filter keeps only star-import noise everywhere and dead-store ('assigned to but never used') messages inside components/; every other finding there now fails the job. The two unused imports were removed.

title: pyflakes (the CI lint step) fails at HEAD: six unused local bindings in recipes_deck0
evidence: python -m pyflakes tools: 'local variable table/pod/sofa/sofa/beds/xm is assigned to but never used' (the lint step filters only star-import messages outside components/, so the python job was red).
impact: Python CI job fails before the unit tests run.
fix: Dropped the unused bindings (the calls are kept; the list comprehension used purely for side effects became a for loop; `xm` removed from the tuple).
resolution: pyflakes over tools/tests/blender is clean apart from the allowed star-import messages; tests/test_regress_python.py P040 (no no-op statements) stays green.

title: Unused imports (line_interval, draw_fittings_section) and dead locals (nac, hb) in the drawing sheets
evidence: pyflakes: "'shipmodel.line_interval' imported but unused", "'hullview.draw_fittings_section' imported but unused", "local variable 'nac' / 'hb' is assigned to but never used".
impact: Lint step red; dead code suggests missing hull-section content.
fix: Removed the unused names; draft tests unchanged.
resolution: Covered by the pyflakes gate of A010/A011; python3 -m unittest discover -s tests green.

title: README quotes stale model/deck/room/door/light counts
evidence: README: '1000-model component library', 'three-deck hull', 'Three decks, 43 rooms ... 26 sliding doors', '~170 real-time lights', '11 component modules, 93 families', '1000 GLBs'. Actual: build_all prints '1198 models in 108 categories', ship.json has 5 decks, 68 rooms, 34 doors, 322 room lights, 19 component module files.
impact: Readers (and the numbers in the CI mermaid chart) contradict the shipped data.
fix: Counts updated to the real values.
resolution: tests/test_regress_assets.py::DocsAndCiAgree checks README against catalog.json and ship.json.

title: CONVENTIONS.md says the family labels sum to exactly 1000; build_all.TARGET is 1198
evidence: build_all.py:26 TARGET = 1198 (1000 + 196 food + 2 signs) and `build_all.py` exits with an error otherwise; CONVENTIONS.md and ARCH.md still say 1000.
impact: A new component author following the documented budget breaks the build.
fix: Docs state 1198 and explain the split.

title: The starcart tour camera stands inside a comms chair (test_camera_eyes_and_spawn_are_not_inside_props fails at HEAD)
evidence: CAMERA_OVERRIDES['starcart'] = (6.5, 13.62, -9.3); ship.json places seat_comms_chair at (6.552, -9.704) (OBB contains the eye point). tests/test_shiplib.py::test_camera_eyes_and_spawn_are_not_inside_props failed on a clean checkout of the integrator tree.
impact: The first-person tour screenshot for that room is taken from inside a chair; a red test on the integrator branch.
fix: Camera moved to x = 5.6 (clear floor), same target.
